item.title: Aerospace Manufacturing - February 2026
item.description: See the future of aerospace and defense manufacturing in this compendium of articles from the editors of Tech Briefs and Aerospace & Defense Technology magazines.

item.title: Wearable Lets Users Control Machines and Robots While on the Move
item.description: Engineers at the University of California San Diego have developed a next-generation wearable system that enables people to control machines using everyday gestures — even while running, riding in a car, or floating on turbulent ocean waves.

item.title: Resource-Sharing Boosts Robotic Resilience
item.description: If the goal of a robot is to perform a function, then minimizing the possibility of failure is a top priority when it comes to robotic design. But although systems with multiple units, or agents, can perform more diverse functions, they also have more different parts that can potentially fail.

item.title: What Robots Can Learn from Sea Stars
item.description: Sea stars are creatures whose movements involve the coordination of hundreds of tiny tube feet to navigate complex environments — despite the lack of a central brain. In other words, it’s as though each foot has a mind of its own.

item.title: Teaching a Robot to Hang a T-shirt Starts with Data
item.description: Building on her experience volunteering at retirement homes, Carnegie Mellon researcher Jasmine Li decided to focus her research on assistive robotics that help people with everyday tasks. “I was interested in the side of robotics that helps people who might not be as familiar with technology,” she said. “I was thinking about the hardware side of robotics, but I ended up doing a lot more with the data collection and software — the algorithmic side.”

item.title: MEMS Device R&D
item.description: Achieving accurate representations of the interactions at play in MEMS devices requires multiphysics simulation. Check out the following ebook, MEMS Device R&D, for four stories on how organizations around the world are using modeling and simulation with the COMSOL® software to develop, analyze, and optimize MEMS devices.

item.title: Meet ULIS: A Power Module with Unprecedented Efficiency, Power Density, and Manufacturability Cost
item.description: Global energy demands are surging, pushed by energy-intensive data centers powering artificial intelligence and increased manufacturing. How will the world meet these rising energy needs?

item.title: Advantages of Smart Power Distribution Unit Design for Automotive & Transportation
item.description: Engineers face increasing pressure to design power distribution units (PDU) that can support higher complexity, greater electrification, and stricter safety demands to support the transition toward more advanced E/E architectures. These rapid shifts are reshaping expectations across the automotive and transportation industries, making innovative PDU design essential for reliability, efficiency, and competitive differentiation.

item.title: Quiet, Please: NVH Improvement Opportunities in the Early Design Cycle
item.description: Noise, vibration, and harshness (NVH) is critical in cars because it directly shapes the driver and passenger experience. This 60-minute webinar from the editors of Automotive Engineering will explore NVH from source to path to recipient, providing engineers and automotive professionals with new insights into how to level up performance and customer satisfaction. item.title: Staining Technique Could Advance Li-ion Batteries
item.description: Researchers at the University of Oxford have developed a powerful new method to visualize an essential Li-ion battery electrode component that had been extremely difficult to trace before. The discovery, published in Nature Communications, could lead to increased manufacturing efficiency of battery electrodes and ultimately help improve the charging rate and lifetime of Li-ion batteries.
